events.title: Trump–Xi Washington state visit and White House summit
events.why_it_matters: Highest-stakes US–China event of the quarter: possible ~$30bn '30-by-30' tariff cuts and Busan-truce extension versus Taiwan arms, rare earths, AI guardrails, and the new Graham secondary-tariff law.
events.what_to_watch: Xi arrives tonight; formal bilateral and state dinner are 9/24 — watch whether the $14bn Taiwan package is delayed and whether any tariff/AI text is issued.

events.title: US–Iran UNGA talks on reopening Hormuz
events.why_it_matters: Witkoff/Kushner–Araghchi shuttle talks and Iran's conditions (lift blockade, unfreeze assets, end 'resistance' fronts) are the first real diplomatic path to collapsing the Hormuz war premium.
events.what_to_watch: Pezeshkian's 9/23 UNGA speech, any Trump–Pezeshkian bilateral, and whether Brent holds the dip below $100 or snaps back on a walk-away.

events.title: Pezeshkian UNGA address; possible Trump–Iran sideline
events.why_it_matters: Iranian President Pezeshkian speaks today after Trump's 9/22 'deal or annihilate' speech and a three-hour US–Iran contact, so rhetoric vs. diplomacy can reprice oil intra-day.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Rubio/Trump green-light a leader-level meeting and whether Iran repeats a ~7-day Hormuz reopen if the US eases the blockade.

events.title: Hormuz tanker war still live; Brent ~$98–100
events.why_it_matters: Physical Hormuz flows remain a fraction of pre-war norms after mid-September tanker hits; even with talks, the war premium still feeds G3 inflation and the Warsh extra-hike path.
events.what_to_watch: Transit counts vs. pre-war 15–20 mb/d, VLCC MEG–China freight, and whether Brent stays sub-$100 on diplomacy or reclaims $101+ on a new strike.

events.title: FDA advisory vote on GRAIL Galleri multi-cancer blood test
events.why_it_matters: A PMA vote on Galleri is the highest-profile diagnostics catalyst in this window and a read-through for MCED reimbursement and Illumina/GRAIL-related healthcare multiples.
events.what_to_watch: Panel vote on safety/effectiveness and any FDA staff concerns that would delay approval into 2027.

events.title: Amaero IPO prices; Bamboo Insurance postponed
events.why_it_matters: Bamboo's ~$665m homeowners-MGU deal was pulled 9/22 on volatility, leaving only the small Amaero industrial listing as today's risk-appetite test.
events.what_to_watch: Amaero aftermarket and whether Bamboo is rescheduled after the Trump–Xi window.

events.title: Costco Q4 FY2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Largest S&P 500 print this week and a high-frequency read on US traffic/mix with gasoline and food inflation still sticky from Hormuz.
events.what_to_watch: Consensus ~$6.53–6.55 EPS and ~$94.9bn sales; comps ex-gas, membership-fee growth, and any tariff/cost commentary.

events.title: SpaceX (SPCX) Day-105 lockup tranche ~328m shares
events.why_it_matters: Fourth staggered post-IPO unlock (~7% of the 180-day block) lands the same day as Trump–Xi and Costco, adding supply into a still-thin mega-IPO float.
events.what_to_watch: SPCX borrow/volume around the unlock and whether the 9/24 FCC satellite-spectrum meeting is used as a positive offset.

events.title: August new-home sales
events.why_it_matters: Confirms whether the housing crack (existing sales 3.98m, starts 1.275m) is spreading into new-home demand after the Warsh hike.
events.what_to_watch: Sales SAAR vs. July, months' supply, and incentive/price cuts that would signal builders absorbing higher mortgage rates.

events.title: BoJ 1.25% policy rate becomes effective
events.why_it_matters: Highest BoJ rate in 31 years (7-2 vote on 9/18) starts transmitting into JGB/yen funding just as G3 tightening is otherwise done for this window.
events.what_to_watch: USD/JPY and whether Takaichi's dovish camp signals a pause after two 2026 hikes.

events.title: US Section 338 import bans on selected Canadian goods
events.why_it_matters: Sept 8 proclamations convert parts of the 50% Canada tit-for-tat into outright bans on specified beer/wine/spirits, some dairy/whey, and large motorcycles at 12:01 a.m. ET Sept 29.
events.what_to_watch: Any last-minute carve-outs or Canadian dollar-for-dollar retaliation beyond the ~$20bn already in force.

events.title: August JOLTS job openings
events.why_it_matters: Opens the labor week into NFP; consensus ~7.2 million openings after July's ~7.3 million, a gauge of how much tightness the Warsh Fed still sees.
events.what_to_watch: Openings vs. 7.2m and quits rate; a sub-7.0m print would challenge the extra 2026 hike in the SEP.

events.title: August PCE / personal income (plus Q2 GDP third estimate)
events.why_it_matters: First post-Warsh inflation print: consensus clusters around core PCE +0.25–0.28% m/m and ~3.3–3.4% y/y, with NIPA annual-update revisions that could shave y/y by 0.1–0.2pp and reprice the extra 2026 hike.
events.what_to_watch: Core m/m vs. 0.25% and whether NIPA revisions cut the y/y; a 0.30%+ core would lock in October/December hike odds.

events.title: Micron fiscal Q4 2026 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Only mega-semiconductor bellwether in this window; HBM/AI memory demand versus China export-control and Trump–Xi AI-guardrail risk.
events.what_to_watch: HBM guidance, China mix, and any comment on export licenses after the 9/24 summit.

events.title: China NBS September PMIs
events.why_it_matters: Official manufacturing/non-manufacturing stayed sub-50 in August (49.8 / 49.0); a third contraction month into the Trump–Xi visit would pressure Beijing for stimulus the PBoC has refused via LPR.
events.what_to_watch: Manufacturing back above 50 vs. another sub-50 print; construction sub-index is the property tell.

events.title: Oura (~$2.1bn) and Accelevation IPOs
events.why_it_matters: Largest remaining US listing in the window (~50m shares at $40–44, mostly secondary) is a post-summit risk-appetite test after Bamboo was pulled.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Oura prices at/above $40–44 and trades well; a pull would confirm the IPO window is shut until after PCE/NFP.

events.title: FCC open meeting on satellite spectrum
events.why_it_matters: Items include unlocking 12.7 GHz and 42 GHz satellite spectrum and UWB modernization — a direct SpaceX/satellite-broadband catalyst on lockup day+6.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the Commission actually votes to free the bands or kicks them to further notice.

events.title: Accenture FY2026 Q4 earnings
events.why_it_matters: IT-services/AI-spending bellwether for enterprise capex after G3 tightening; bookings will show whether AI projects are still funded into a higher-for-longer Warsh path.
events.what_to_watch: New bookings, FY27 guidance, and consulting vs. managed-services mix.

events.title: Nike Q1 FY2027 earnings
events.why_it_matters: Global consumer/China-demand read one week after Trump–Xi; consensus ~$0.44–0.45 EPS and ~$11.35bn sales (down YoY).
events.what_to_watch: Greater China sales, inventory/promotions, and any tariff commentary after the summit.

events.title: ISM manufacturing PMI (September)
events.why_it_matters: August ISM manufacturing was a firm 54.6; a fade toward the ~53.5 flash would show G3 tightening and Hormuz costs hitting factory orders.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs. 54.6, prices-paid, and new orders.

events.title: Caixin China manufacturing PMI (September)
events.why_it_matters: Private-sector PMI is the cleaner export/new-order read one week after Trump–Xi and usually prints the first working day of October.
events.what_to_watch: New export orders vs. the still-soft NBS official series.

events.title: September employment report (NFP)
events.why_it_matters: Last labor print before the Oct 27–28 FOMC; consensus has drifted toward ~+90k (from ~+120k) with unemployment ~4.3%, deciding whether the Warsh majority's extra 25bp by year-end stays priced.
events.what_to_watch: Payrolls vs. 90–120k, unemployment vs. 4.3%, and average hourly earnings; a sub-75k / 4.4% combo would fade the extra hike.

events.title: Eurozone September HICP flash
events.why_it_matters: August HICP jumped to 3.2% y/y on 14.3% energy inflation after the ECB's 9/10 hike to DF 2.50%; the flash is the first test of whether Hormuz is still lifting euro inflation into the 10/29 meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs. 3.2% and core vs. 2.4%; another energy spike keeps October 'live' for Lagarde.

events.title: OPEC+ seven-country meeting on November quotas
events.why_it_matters: The core seven held October quotas unchanged on 9/6 after finishing the 1.65 mb/d unwind; Nov policy is the first OPEC response to Hormuz talks and ~$99 Brent.
events.what_to_watch: Hold vs. a symbolic cut if diplomacy fails, and any 2027 baseline/quota language.

events.title: ISM services PMI (September)
events.why_it_matters: August services ISM was 55.4; with retail already rebounding +1.2%, a sub-54 print would be the first sign the Warsh hike is hitting the dominant side of the economy.
events.what_to_watch: Headline vs. 55.4 and prices-paid vs. employment.

events.title: September FOMC minutes (Warsh hike / extra-dot debate)
events.why_it_matters: Minutes of the unanimous 25bp hike to 3.75–4.00% will show how hard the 12-of-18 extra-2026-hike majority pushed versus a one-and-done camp.
events.what_to_watch: Language on energy/Hormuz as a 'look-through' shock vs. a reason to keep hiking; any dissent-in-discussion despite the 12-0 vote.

events.title: Paramount–WBD merger close window
events.why_it_matters: FCC foreign-ownership waiver (9/17) plus a 9/21 state antitrust settlement put the ~$110bn deal on a ~two-week close path, reshaping US TV/streaming concentration.
events.what_to_watch: Close announcement vs. any last Tunney/state-holdup; CNN/CBS editorial-board conditions.

events.title: Live Nation/Ticketmaster Tunney Act judgment window
events.why_it_matters: Public comment ended 9/4; a mid-September-to-mid-October entry of the behavioral settlement (no breakup) would lock in the live-events market structure.
events.what_to_watch: Whether the judge accepts DOJ's no-divestiture deal or sides with states still seeking a Ticketmaster split.

events.title: UNGA 81: Trump address and whirlwind bilaterals
events.why_it_matters: Trump's opening-day speech defended the Iran war, threatened annihilation absent a deal, and teed up Witkoff–Iran and Zelensky energy-truce talks now driving oil vol.
events.what_to_watch: Resolved as a speech event; residual market effect sits in the live Iran and Ukraine tracks.

events.title: Trump–Zelensky energy-infrastructure truce track
events.why_it_matters: No deal was signed; Zelensky said Ukraine will halt refinery strikes only if Russia stops hitting Ukraine's grid — diesel/refining remains a live midterm story.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Washington actually conveys the proposal to Moscow and if Russian refinery hits pause into October.

events.title: Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act signed
events.why_it_matters: P.L. 119-111 authorizes up to 100% secondary tariffs on top buyers of Russian oil/gas (China/India risk) plus Iran Sanctions Act extension through 2031 — a live overlay on Trump–Xi.
events.what_to_watch: Whether Trump uses or waives the secondary-tariff clock during/after the Xi visit.

events.title: Warsh Fed hikes 25bp to 3.75–4.00%; SEP extra hike
events.why_it_matters: First hike since 2023; 12 of 18 dots show at least one more 25bp in 2026, so PCE (9/30) and NFP (10/2) are the only data that can still reprice the path before Oct 27–28.
events.what_to_watch: Market odds of an October vs. December follow-up; minutes 10/7 for the internal debate.

events.title: ECB hikes 25bp to DF 2.50% on Hormuz inflation
events.why_it_matters: Deposit rate 2.50% effective 9/16; energy-driven HICP at 3.2% keeps October 29 live even though this window has no ECB meeting.
events.what_to_watch: Oct 2 HICP flash; Makhlouf has already called every meeting live.

events.title: PBoC holds 1y/5y LPR at 3.00%/3.50% (16th month)
events.why_it_matters: No rate relief into soft PMIs and a hawkish Fed, so any China impulse into Trump–Xi has to come from fiscal/property, not LPR.
events.what_to_watch: NBS PMI 9/30; a third sub-50 month would revive RRR-cut chatter the PBoC just declined.

events.title: US housing crack vs. August retail rebound
events.why_it_matters: Existing-home sales hit a 2026 low (3.98m) and starts fell to 1.275m even as retail sales jumped +1.2% — the split the Warsh Fed must parse at PCE/NFP.
events.what_to_watch: New-home sales 9/24 and whether mortgage-rate backup after the hike kills the retail rebound.

events.title: FTC appeals Meta Instagram/WhatsApp antitrust loss
events.why_it_matters: Appeal of the Nov 2025 Meta win reopens breakup risk on a long clock; near-term it is a sentiment overhang, not a 2-week price event.
events.what_to_watch: Stay/briefing schedule; no merits ruling is due inside this window.

events.title: Atlantic hurricane season still hurricane-free
events.why_it_matters: El Niño has produced no hurricanes through 9/23 (latest first hurricane on satellite-era record); Gulf oil/gas has had negligible storm losses, so weather is not the oil story — Hormuz is.
events.what_to_watch: NHC basin outlook; season runs to 11/30 but this window looks quiet.

top_risks: Trump–Xi breakdown: Taiwan $14bn arms delay/rare-earth retaliation/no 30-by-30 text, with Graham secondary tariffs hanging over China as a Russian-oil buyer
Hormuz talks fail and another tanker strike sends Brent back through $101–110, feeding Warsh/ECB inflation
Hot August core PCE (≥0.30% m/m) and/or firm NFP locking the extra 2026 Fed hike before Oct 27–28
Canada Section 338 bans (9/29) plus unfinished USMCA tit-for-tat spilling into autos/consumer staples
IPO/lockup supply (SPCX 9/24, Oura 9/30) into a thin post-hike tape if summit optics disappoint
top_opportunities: Credible US–Iran path to reopen Hormuz (Iran floated ~7 days if blockade/assets move) collapsing the oil/diesel premium
Incremental Trump–Xi deliverables: Busan-truce extension, ~$30bn reciprocal tariff cuts, AI hotline — risk-on for China-sensitive cyclicals and semis
Ukraine–Russia energy-infrastructure truce that actually sticks, easing diesel and European refining stress
Soft PCE (core ≤0.22% or NIPA y/y downward revision) fading the extra Warsh hike into Oct 2 NFP
Quiet Atlantic hurricane peak plus OPEC+ on hold, so any Hormuz de-escalation is not offset by Gulf shut-ins or a quota hike
summary: The two-way overlay is now inside 24–48 hours: Xi arrives tonight for a 9/24 White House summit (tariff cuts/AI vs Taiwan arms and the Graham secondary-tariff clock) against still-unresolved Hormuz diplomacy that has already eased Brent from ~$101–102 to ~$98–100. G3 tightening is done for this window (Warsh 3.75–4.00%, BoJ 1.25% effective 9/24, ECB 2.50%), so the data that can still reprice the path are Aug PCE (9/30) and Oct 2 NFP, while US housing is already cracking even as nominal retail sales rebounded +1.2%.
